solverWeights.title: Scheduling weights
solverWeights.intro: These control how the automatic scheduler trades off competing goals when it builds a schedule. A higher number means the scheduler tries harder to avoid that problem, even at the cost of the others. Changing these only affects future runs — past runs keep showing the weights they actually used.

understaffing.label: Avoid leaving shifts understaffed
understaffing.help: How strongly to avoid leaving a shift short of its required staff count. This should almost always be the highest number by far.

contract_min_shortfall.label: Avoid leaving people under their contract minimum
contract_min_shortfall.help: How strongly to avoid giving someone fewer shifts than their contract requires.

denied_preference.label: Try to grant preferred shifts
denied_preference.help: How much extra weight to give someone's "preferred" shifts over shifts they only marked as merely available.

fairness_spread.label: Give everyone a similar number of shifts
fairness_spread.help: How much to prioritise keeping shift counts even across employees, instead of a few people getting far more than others.

unpopular_shift_spread.label: Spread weekend shifts evenly
unpopular_shift_spread.help: How much to prioritise spreading weekend and other unpopular shifts evenly, instead of the same few people always covering them.

score_weight.label: Favor higher-scoring employees for contested shifts
score_weight.help: How much an employee's performance score influences who wins a shift when several people want the same one.

preference_debt.label: Make up for past denied preferences
preference_debt.help: How much to favor someone whose preferred shifts were denied in previous months, so the same people aren't repeatedly passed over.

adminRules.title: Scheduling rules
